summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of Addison’s disease, hypothyroidism, and microscopic colitis was admitted for recurrent diarrhea, abdominal cramping, and lightheadedness consistent with an adrenal insufficiency flare. She was treated with IV fluids, stress-dose hydrocortisone, and symptom management. Stool studies ruled out infectious causes. A colonoscopy showed a normal appearance with biopsies taken to evaluate for microscopic colitis; a small rectal polyp was removed. Her symptoms improved with steroid treatment, and she was discharged on a slow prednisone taper. She will follow up with gastroenterology for biopsy results and outpatient management.
